sections.heading: How to Choose from This List
body: Start by deciding whether you want the cheapest path to more distance or a more balanced premium ball that still offers strong driver-speed upside. The wrong move is chasing a pure distance label when what you really want is a better all-around fit.

sections.heading: What the Tradeoffs Really Are
body: Budget distance balls usually win on price and easy replacement cost, but they give up some refinement in feel. Premium options can preserve a more complete tee-to-green profile, but you pay for that broader fit. The best pick depends on whether you value cheap testing, all-around confidence, or a middle lane between the two.

faqs.question: What type of golf ball usually helps with longer drives?
faqs.answer: Golfers usually look for balls that support fast ball speed and favorable driver launch conditions, but the best fit still depends on swing speed, launch, and how much feel you want to keep.

faqs.question: Is a distance golf ball always better than a premium ball for long drives?
faqs.answer: Not always. Some premium balls still deliver excellent driver distance while giving a more balanced feel and overall performance profile.

faqs.question: Should budget golfers still test premium distance balls?
faqs.answer: Yes, if overall performance matters. But if the goal is simply cheaper extra yards, a budget distance ball can still be the smarter first test.
